demo.aboutSummary: This is the public demo of ANet Drone4D. The shared show runs the 7x24 relay demonstration (scenario S7) continuously and is read-only for every visitor. Each visitor may open one isolated sandbox (30 min initially, renewable up to 120 min) to place drones, targets and nests and to run tasks. Seven worlds are available; the six UrbanScene3D cities are used under authorization from the dataset's rights holders. Frame rate and image quality depend on the visitor's GPU.

landing.story.concept: Concept illustration, not a product screenshot
landing.story.digital-twin.alt: Concept illustration: a small voxel airplane crosses a voxel city model whose near blocks refine into finer detail
landing.story.digital-twin.body: Seven urban worlds stream to the browser as octree point clouds. Point density adapts to the viewpoint and frame budget; a GPU point pool renders the result in a single draw call.
landing.story.digital-twin.p1: ANet Synthetic City and six UrbanScene3D cities
landing.story.digital-twin.p3: CPU build time of 27–35 s per city
landing.story.digital-twin.title: Urban worlds in motion
landing.story.environment.alt: Concept illustration: a voxel airplane crosses wind ribbons and rain above a voxel city
landing.story.environment.body: Wind fields combine vertical profiles and turbulence, while visibility and precipitation define operating conditions. The physics engine samples the environment at 50 Hz across 12 weather presets, from clear skies to sandstorms.
landing.story.environment.title: Weather as simulation state
landing.story.fleet-control.alt: Concept illustration: a voxel airplane leads eight voxel quadcopters in formation over coverage lanes
landing.story.fleet-control.body: FleetSim advances 1 to 1,000 drones on a shared 250 Hz clock, sustaining real-time execution at 1,000 drones on roughly half a CPU core. Flight control combines a PX4-style position-and-attitude cascade, verified against PX4 SIH flight logs, with formation, area coverage, and mission primitives.
landing.story.fleet-control.p1: PX4-lite cascade verified against PX4 SIH logs
landing.story.fleet-control.p2: Formations, area coverage, and eight mission generators
landing.story.fleet-control.p3: Geofences, fleet separation, and a 14-state flight state machine
landing.story.fleet-control.title: One clock for the fleet
landing.story.perception.alt: Concept illustration: a voxel airplane casts a red sampling fan toward a distant target
landing.story.perception.body: Target perception covers six classes—people, drones, machines, dogs, vehicles, and objects—across EO, night-vision, LWIR, LiDAR, radar, and acoustic modalities. Based on Johnson criteria and TTPF, the model outputs sound pressure, angular subtense, equivalent pixels, and detection probability.
landing.story.perception.p1: Six target classes across six sensor modalities
landing.story.perception.p3: Detection probability and underlying physical observables
landing.story.perception.title: From sensing to detection probability
landing.story.relay-agents.alt: Concept illustration: dashed handover routes between three nests as two aircraft complete a relay
landing.story.relay-agents.body: Automated nests use greedy allocation across seven task types and maintain 7×24 relay watch from stations outside each target’s sensitivity range. As physical agents, drones can discover capabilities and delegate tasks over Mock ANet, verified against receipts; this agent-swarm layer is disabled on the public site.
landing.story.relay-agents.p1: Seven task types with greedy allocation
landing.story.relay-agents.p2: 7×24 relay watch from beyond target sensitivity range
landing.story.relay-agents.p3: Receipt-verified agent swarm; disabled on public site
landing.story.relay-agents.title: Coordination beyond single flights
landing.story.roadmap.alt: Concept illustration: a voxel airplane departs a landing pad toward two wireframe stages ahead
landing.story.roadmap.body: In development for V0.3, the D3 Event Lab includes Gazebo Sim lockstep, event-level observation benchmarks, mesh sensors, 4D reconstruction evaluation, and Rerun inspection. A 3DGS appearance layer over mesh geometry and PX4 SITL integration with Gazebo remain research directions, not available features.
landing.story.roadmap.p1: Gazebo Sim lockstep and event-level benchmarks
landing.story.roadmap.p2: Livox MID-360-pattern mesh LiDAR, mesh cameras, FAST-LIVO2 evaluation against mesh ground truth, and Rerun inspection
landing.story.roadmap.title: Next tiers of simulation fidelity
landing.story.sandbox.body: Each session provisions an isolated simulation core for up to 12 drones, 30 targets, and 4 nests. The sandbox supports desktop browsers, phones, and tablets, with a REST v1 API and Python SDK; each UrbanScene3D city also includes a recorded drone-monitoring demonstration.
landing.story.sandbox.p1: Up to 12 drones, 30 targets, and 4 nests per sandbox
landing.story.sandbox.p2: Admission control, live queue visibility, and energy-saving mode
landing.story.sandbox.p3: No server GPU required; browser-side rendering
landing.story.sandbox.title: An isolated core for each visitor
landing.story.sub: From point-cloud worlds to the next tiers of simulation fidelity, one voxel airplane carries the story through every capability.
landing.story.title: Seven chapters, one flight path
